clue.text: Kind person

blocks.note: first meaning: a sort or category
second meaning: an individual of a particular character, as in 'the quiet sort'

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a kind-hearted person, but 'Kind' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a category or sort and, informally, an individual with a given character, as in 'an outdoor sort'.

clue.text: Theatrical type, he's covered in applied paint

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is enclosed by it, so these letters sit inside the other
applied paint is spread about rather than left as it was, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor caked in greasepaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' reads as describing the paint on the actor's face, but it tells you to rearrange that word, and the rearrangement is then split around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, named after Thespis, the supposed founder of Greek drama.

clue.text: Vegetables of equal value, bargains

blocks.note: at par means at equal value
a snip is British slang for a bargain

explanation.surface: Vegetables all priced the same, and cheap at that, like a market stall offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables related to the carrot, so they are one example of the class.

clue.text: Playing Chopin, us in a small pad

indicators.note: playing a piece is performing it, here read as rearranging the letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pianist performing Chopin for us in a small flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing Chopin' sets up a recital, and 'pad' suggests a modest apartment; the first 'in' is fodder, the second the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincushion is a small stuffed cushion into which sewing pins are stuck for storage.

clue.text: Model of one Kent resort

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: A scale model of a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to follow, the same sense as a model of behaviour.

clue.text: Lucas sets out swords

indicators.note: letters that are out are put out of place, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Lucas laying out his weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlasses are short curved swords, traditionally carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Say something you shouldn't have said? Many times during reversal of policy after summit in Somalia

definitions.text: Say something you shouldn't have said?

indicators.note: a thing in another is held within it, so the summit sits inside the country's code
something during another happens within its span, so one word is set inside the other
one piece after another is placed behind it, so this group comes second

blocks.note: SO is the international country code for Somalia
a summit is a peak
a U-turn is a complete change of policy
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A news item about a government abruptly changing course after a summit meeting held in Somalia.
explanation.walkthrough: Both insertions happen first and the two halves are then joined; the second insertion lands mid-word, after the first two letters of the policy reversal. Somalia's two-letter country code is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak out of turn is an idiom for saying something tactless or inappropriate for one's position.

clue.text: Slim and fit with trendy haircut

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a trim is a light haircut

explanation.surface: Someone lean and healthy showing off a fashionable new hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in trim is an idiom for being in good physical condition.

clue.text: Provoke pointer

blocks.note: first meaning: to irritate or goad someone
second meaning: the indicator on a dial or compass

explanation.walkthrough: 'pointer' suggests a breed of dog that could be provoked; it is the gauge's indicating arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for goading someone and a noun for the indicator on an instrument dial.

clue.text: Material for building modern plant etc

indicators.note: building something means assembling it from parts, so these letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supply list of what is needed to construct a new factory and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material for building' reads as one phrase, but 'building' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Portland cement is the standard construction binder, named for its resemblance to Portland stone.

clue.text: An opening for a listener in the east with a part to play around hospital

indicators.note: something placed around another item encloses it, so the role wraps the hospital letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
taken as written
an actor's part is a role
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Describing something like a theatre box: a spot in the east of the building for someone who listens while playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: E and A come first, then ROLE goes around H to give RHOLE: E + A + RHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An earhole is, informally, the ear's opening, the passage through which a listener hears sound.

clue.text: Article, a piece of tosh about playhouse

indicators.note: a piece of something is only a small part of it, here just its opening letter

blocks.note: the definite article
taken as written
the first letter of tosh
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper article dismissing some piece as rubbish about a playhouse, like a sniffy review.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building where plays are staged, which is what a theatre is.

clue.text: Old man receiving an order that includes a cigar

indicators.note: a person receiving something takes it in, so the old man's letters hold what follows
something that includes another thing holds it within, so the order takes in a letter

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
the 'a' that the order includes
to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: An elderly man being handed an order that comes with a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'a' is included between the first two inner pieces, and the old man then goes around the lot; 'Old man' is father, not an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long, slender cigar, so the general word names it as one example.

clue.text: Finish off snapping tail of lobster, seafood

indicators.note: snapping means seizing in the jaws, so one word catches and holds the other letter
the tail of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to finish off is to kill
the last letter of lobster

explanation.surface: Killing a lobster by snapping off its tail before serving it as seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside KILL after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny marine crustaceans, eaten by whales and sometimes by people, so they count as seafood.

clue.text: A confusing series of letters from boy reportedly assists Oxford publisher

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so a word is spelt from its spoken form

blocks.note: Alf is a boy's name, spelt here as it is pronounced in a different way
to abet is to assist
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A puzzling string of letters received from a lad said to be helping an Oxford publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the soup with pasta letters in it, used figuratively for a bewildering mass of acronyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabet soup figuratively means a confusing jumble of abbreviations and initials, from the pasta-letter soup.

clue.text: Watch batsman, perhaps, in wonder

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it
in cricket an opener is a batsman who starts the innings

explanation.surface: A spectator gazing in amazement at a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen are the first pair to bat in an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, a thing that makes one marvel.

clue.text: Lacking knowledge, ranting stupidly about love

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it senselessly, so the letters lose their order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the love symbol

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone uninformed foolishly sounding off about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant describes someone without education or awareness, the condition of having no information.

clue.text: Envy bum on Dickens character

blocks.note: to bum is to cadge or beg
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Jealousy aimed at some Dickensian figure's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the noun for a backside; it is the verb meaning to cadge. In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it, a form of jealousy.

clue.text: Fern in ground seated poorly

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fern sitting awkwardly in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Adder's tongue is a small fern named for its spore-bearing spike, which resembles a snake's tongue.

clue.text: Maiden on racecourse - good luck charm required

blocks.note: in cricket scoring M stands for a maiden over
Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A young woman at the races who needs a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good fortune to a team or group.

clue.text: Conspicuous beacon

blocks.note: first meaning: striking or notable
second meaning: a light or sign used to give warning

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a beacon that stands out; the adjective sense is the less familiar one, as in 'a signal achievement'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means striking or remarkable; as a noun it is a sign or light conveying a message.

clue.text: Girl that might front band?

blocks.note: surface reading: a young woman who could be lead singer of a pop group
setter's reading: a girl's name that goes in front of the word band to make a kind of hairband

explanation.walkthrough: An Alice band is a broad headband worn over the hair, named after Alice in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name precedes 'band' in the name of a headband, so it literally stands at the front of band.

clue.text: Wine in inn poor - it must be changed

indicators.note: what must be changed has to be altered, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the wine at a pub is bad and has to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like the complaint about the wine but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it, especially in Burgundy.

clue.text: Aristocratic head, the Parisian

blocks.note: nob is slang for the head
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Describing a Paris-born head of some grand family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nob' also means a toff, which suits the aristocratic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes someone belonging to the hereditary titled class, the aristocracy.

clue.text: Business interest

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm or company
second meaning: a matter one cares about or is involved in

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single commercial phrase, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a commercial firm and for a matter that engages someone or affects them.

clue.text: Local girl, not quite insane, needs help

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: barmy is British slang for mad
aid means help

explanation.surface: A girl from the neighbourhood, a bit unhinged, who needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub, so a local girl serves drinks there; it is not about a girl from the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is a woman serving drinks behind a bar, and the local is a regular pub.

clue.text: Don't mince words in republic following speech

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the country is placed second

blocks.note: a talk is a speech
Turkey is a republic

explanation.surface: Advice to speak bluntly when delivering an address in some republic.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom meaning to discuss something frankly and directly, without evasion.

clue.text: Filthy place close to lane, an eyesore

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a pigsty, or any dirty place
the last letter of lane

explanation.surface: A grubby spot by a lane that is ugly to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' usually means an ugly sight; here it is read literally as a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.
